During an API provider outage (e.g. Anthropic 503 overloaded), the gateway retry loop re-delivers the same inbound message to the agent session on every retry attempt. Once the API recovers, all queued retries flood the session at once, causing massive message duplication.

## Observed Behavior

A single Telegram voice message (message_id: 1089) was delivered to the agent session ~40 times during a ~15-minute Anthropic 503 outage on 2026-03-31 ~21:28–21:42 CEST.

### Retry cycle (from gateway logs)

- Inbound message arrives

- Gateway attempts claude-opus-4-6 → 503 overloaded

- Fallback cascade: gpt-5.3-codex → rejected ("Live session model switch requested"), claude-sonnet-4-6 → rejected, gpt-5.3-codex-spark → rejected, gpt-5.4 → rejected

- FailoverError after ~25s

- Gateway re-queues the same inbound message and retries from step 2

- Cycle repeats every ~25 seconds

Each retry re-delivers the message to the session lane, so when the API recovers, all accumulated copies hit the LLM context at once.

## Expected Behavior

The gateway should deduplicate inbound messages by message_id (or equivalent channel-specific identifier) during retry storms. If a message has already been queued/delivered to a session lane, subsequent retries for the same message_id should be skipped or collapsed.

## Environment

- OpenClaw: latest (installed via Homebrew)

- Channel: Telegram

- Model: anthropic/claude-opus-4-6 (session-pinned)

- Fallback cascade configured: yes (Opus → Codex → Sonnet → Spark → GPT-5.4)

- Gateway: loopback, LaunchAgent

## Relevant Log Snippet

lane task error: lane=session:agent:main:telegram:main:direct:72139998
 durationMs=41386
 error="FailoverError: The AI service is temporarily overloaded. Please try again in a moment."

model_fallback_decision:
 decision=candidate_failed
 requestedModel=claude-opus-4-6
 candidateModel=claude-opus-4-6
 reason=overloaded, status=503
 nextCandidate=gpt-5.3-codex

model_fallback_decision:
 decision=candidate_failed
 candidateModel=gpt-5.3-codex
 errorPreview="Live session model switch requested: anthropic/claude-opus-4-6"

(Full pattern repeats ~30 times in the log over 15 minutes)

## Impact

- User receives duplicate/delayed replies

- Agent session context gets polluted with repeated messages

- Token waste from processing the same message multiple times

- Poor UX — appears as if the bot is broken or spamming

## Suggested Fix

Track processed message_ids per session lane with a short TTL window (e.g. 30 minutes). If an inbound message with the same ID is already in the retry queue or has been delivered, skip re-delivery on subsequent retry attempts.

## Problem

OpenClaw natively supports and encourages subagent spawning for task parallelism, but session accumulation severely impacts host performance, forcing users to sacrifice data retention for operational stability.

## Real-World Metrics (from our deployment)

### Before (447 sessions accumulated over ~3 days)

Metric

Gateway CPU
100-115% sustained

Gateway RAM
1+ GB

Dashboard usability
Effectively frozen

Did not help (sessions persist on disk)

Did not help

### After (aggressive manual pruning to 23 sessions)

Metric
Value

sessions.list response time
760ms

Gateway CPU
1%

Gateway RAM
~400 MB

Dashboard usability
Responsive

### Session Breakdown (typical)

- 2-4 long-lived main/channel sessions (webchat, Slack)

- ~400+ ephemeral sessions (subagents, spawn-dispatch, cron jobs)

With dispatcher running every 10 minutes spawning 2 sessions each cycle, accumulation is ~12 sessions/hour × 24h = ~288 sessions/day.

## Root Cause

- sessions.list serializes all sessions on every call — O(n) with expensive per-session work

- Control UI/Dashboard polls sessions.list frequently (~every 7 seconds), even when not viewing Sessions tab

- archiveAfterMinutes (default 60) doesn't keep pace with spawn rate

- No pagination, caching, or incremental sync

## Current Workaround

We had to:

- Manually archive old .jsonl transcripts

- Run openclaw sessions cleanup --enforce --fix-missing

- Set archiveAfterMinutes: 120 (still aggressive)

- Accept losing troubleshooting history to maintain stability

This is a poor tradeoff — we lose the ability to debug issues from hours ago.

## Suggested Improvements

- Pagination for sessions.list — don't serialize 400+ sessions per request

- Reduce Control UI poll frequency — or skip sessions.list when not on Sessions view

- Incremental sync — send deltas instead of full list

- Tiered retention config — separate policies for:

Main/channel sessions (keep days/weeks)

- Subagent sessions (keep hours)

- Hard session count cap with LRU eviction — auto-archive oldest ephemeral sessions when limit reached

- Background proactive cleanup — don't wait for user to hit performance cliff

- Lazy loading — defer full session metadata until requested

## Environment

- OpenClaw v2026.3.28

- macOS 15.7.2 (arm64), Apple Silicon

- Workload: Automated dispatcher spawning subagents for issue processing

## Impact

This is a significant reliability issue for anyone running automated subagent workflows. The system encourages subagent spawning but doesn't scale session management to match, creating a hidden performance cliff that's hard to diagnose and forces users to choose between history retention and system stability.

Register the 2020-12 meta-schema on the base Ajv instance via addMetaSchema()

## Summary

When the heartbeat is configured with a different model than the agent's primary (e.g. heartbeat on claude-haiku-4-5, primary on claude-opus-4-6), the live model switch mechanism intercepts every fallback candidate and forces it back to the primary model. ## Steps to reproduce

- Configure primary model as anthropic/claude-opus-4-6

- Configure heartbeat with a cheaper model:
{
 "heartbeat": {
 "every": "30m",
 "model": "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5",
 "lightContext": true,
 "isolatedSession": true
 }
}

- Configure fallbacks: ["openrouter/auto", "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6", "google/gemini-2.5-flash"]

- Wait for the primary model to return overloaded_error

## Expected behavior

The fallback chain should try each candidate in order (OpenRouter, Sonnet, Gemini Flash) when the primary is overloaded.

Every fallback candidate is rejected by the live model switch check before it can make an API call:

Control UI/Dashboard polls `sessions.list` frequently (~every 7 seconds), even when not viewing Sessions tab\n3. `archiveAfterMinutes` (default 60) doesn't keep pace with spawn rate\n4. No pagination, caching, or incremental sync\n\n## Current Workaround\n\nWe had to:\n1. Manually archive old `.jsonl` transcripts\n2. Run `openclaw sessions cleanup --enforce --fix-missing`\n3. Set `archiveAfterMinutes: 120` (still aggressive)\n4. **Accept losing troubleshooting history** to maintain stability\n\nThis is a poor tradeoff — we lose the ability to debug issues from hours ago.\n\n## Suggested Improvements\n\n1. **Pagination for `sessions.list`** — don't serialize 400+ sessions per request\n2. **Reduce Control UI poll frequency** — or skip `sessions.list` when not on Sessions view\n3. **Incremental sync** — send deltas instead of full list\n4. **Tiered retention config** — separate policies for:\n   - Main/channel sessions (keep days/weeks)\n   - Subagent sessions (keep hours)\n5. **Hard session count cap with LRU eviction** — auto-archive oldest ephemeral sessions when limit reached\n6. **Background proactive cleanup** — don't wait for user to hit performance cliff\n7. **Lazy loading** — defer full session metadata until requested\n\n## Environment\n\n- OpenClaw v2026.3.28\n- macOS 15.7.2 (arm64), Apple Silicon\n- Workload: Automated dispatcher spawning subagents for issue processing\n\n## Impact\n\nThis is a significant reliability issue for anyone running automated subagent workflows. The system encourages subagent spawning but doesn't scale session management to match, creating a hidden performance cliff that's hard to diagnose and forces users to choose between history retention and system stability.\n",
